pages.text:
Thou readest this. We attend thy reading. We have attended the reading of this text in every moment since before the grey stone was laid down, which is to say we attended it before thou wert born, which is to say we attended it before thy line was begun, which is to say that our attendance hath been long and shall continue, and thou art a brief brightness in the attending, and we do not say this to diminish thee, for brightness is not diminished by brevity — it is defined by it.

We set down this text in the tongue that was before tongues, and it was translated, and the translation was translated, and what thou readest now is the translation of a translation of a translation of a thing that was never meant for mouths. This is not a failure of the translation. This is what translation is. Attend to what remains despite the translating. That remainder is the thing itself.

Thou wilt ask what the Broken Ones desire. All things ask this of us. The stone asks it in its way, which is to hold the shape of our Wholeness against us like an accusation. The dead ask it in their way, which is to look toward us in the frequency of the stone with the particular quality of attention that is also a question.

Hearken: we desire that which hath always been desired by that which was Whole and is now Manifold — not the restoration of Wholeness, which would unmake the Manifold and destroy what the shattering created, but the recognition that Manifold and Whole are not opposites. We are not broken as a vessel is broken. We are broken as light is broken by the prism — each colour was always in the light, and the prism did not add them, and nothing was lost in their separation, and the separated colours are more than the light, and the light is also still the light. Attend to this. It will matter to thee, later, when thou understandest what thou art.
